OR 0.4941 (0.3466 to 0.7045), 95% interval

Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Number of Subjects With Severe Rotavirus Gastroenteritis (rv ge) Caused by the Circulating Wild-type Rotavirus Strain | Occurrence of Severe Clinical Rotavirus Disease Caused by Any Rotavirus Serotype More Than 14 Days Following the Third D. random-effects, estimator REML (restricted maximum likelihood), k = 3.

τ² 0.05718 · I² 57.62% · Q 4.72 on 2 df

Favours: the intervention (lower is better)

not recorded on the page this object was extracted from

The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason.

A published individual-level analysis argues this kind of estimate is biased toward the null by the setting it was measured in. Amin et al., American Journal of Epidemiology 2025 (PMID 39745811), pooled 83,592 infants across 23 countries from monovalent rotavirus vaccine trials. Efficacy against severe rotavirus gastroenteritis appeared to vary from 10% to 100% between countries; after adjusting for local exposure magnitude, all but two countries fell between 80% and 86%. High-burden settings -- which include the African settings pooled here -- are where the unadjusted estimates are lowest.

That analysis held the vaccine class constant (monovalent) and modelled the setting. This pool combines Rotarix, RotaTeq and Rotasiil -- three different vaccines -- and pools across settings. The two designs answer different questions and theirs isolates a cause.

Their 80-86% and this pool's ~51% are not two estimates of one quantity: one is exposure-adjusted single-vaccine efficacy, the other is unadjusted multi-vaccine. The finding is about design, not about a number being wrong.

Read this beside the estimate. The unadjusted interval is OR 0.4941 (0.3466 to 0.7045) and excludes no effect. This project's hartung-knapp interval at k = 3 IS 0.2268 TO 1.0764, on t = 4.3027 with 2 degrees of freedom, and it includes no effect. The house rule already requires the adjusted interval to be shown beside the unadjusted one where k is small; on this pool the two disagree about the conclusion.

Stated so the caution is not discounted. At k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and almost no effect survives the adjustment, so a crossing there is weak evidence. Here k = 3 and t IS 4.3027, which is a far less demanding test. There is also real spread: tau-squared 0.0557, Q 4.7195 on 2 df, I-squared 56.97%. The crossing is driven by disagreement between the trials, not by the correction being brutal at tiny k.

The stored estimate is not changed. Withdrawing or restating a published number is a content decision. What has been done is to put the adjusted interval where a reader meets the number.

Read this beside the estimate. The three trials administered three different vaccines, verified against their registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT00241644 gave Rotarix, a monovalent human vaccine; NCT00362648 gave RotaTeq, a pentavalent human-bovine reassortant; NCT02145000 gave BRV-PV, a pentavalent bovine vaccine. They differ in valency, in strain origin and in manufacturer. A single pooled odds ratio across them estimates the average effect of three products, not the effect of a rotavirus vaccine, and a reader deciding about one product cannot take this number as its efficacy. I-squared is 57.6%, which is consistent with that and does not establish it.

The stored point is 0.4940987113879037 on an interval running from 0.347 to 0.704. Fifteen of those sixteen digits are noise: the interval is 0.36 wide, so the estimate is not determined beyond the second decimal place. Reporting it at sixteen figures asserts a precision the data cannot carry, and it is the same defect as a displayed value the engine could not compute -- a number saying more than its evidence. The value is not rounded here, because it is a published number; what is recorded is that it should be read as 0.49 (0.35 to 0.70).

What this pool holds constant

Table 5. What this pool holds constant
DimensionAcross the pooled cohortsIf it differs, why it is crossed anyway
effect measureESTABLISHEDodds ratio for severe rotavirus gastroenteritis
estimandESTABLISHED WITH A STATED VARIANCEAll three trials measure severe rotavirus gastroenteritis -- the same construct. The case definition differs in strain inclusion: NCT00241644 counts disease caused by circulating wild-type strains; NCT00362648 counts disease caused by any rotavirus serotype; NCT02145000 counts laboratory-confirmed severe rotavirus gastroenteritis. A wild-type-only definition excludes vaccine-strain shedding that an any-serotype definition includes, so the denominators of disease are not identical. Not incommensurable constructs -- a definitional variance within one construct, declared rather than withdrawn.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 8. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as publishedREML (restricted maximum likelihood)0.4941 (0.3466 to 0.7045)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 2 degree(s) of freedom (t = 4.3027)0.4941 (0.2268 to 1.0764)

The published point is 0.4941 and the house-rule point is 0.4941. The number a reader remembers does not move; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never narrow an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a known problem with known handling rather than a novel judgement.

  1. No GRADE assessment or reconciliation record is held in this object, so the certainty of this evidence has not been rated. This is recorded as a declared departure under Cochrane Handbook §III.3.4.1: the review reports a pooled estimate for which no certainty assessment was made. Rating it here would require two assessors and an adjudicator, and a rating produced by neither is not a GRADE assessment whatever letter it carries.
  2. Read this beside `estimand_established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the same quantity. It records nothing about what that quantity was measured against -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. On attr-pn-review the flag is true and correct while the pool combines patisiran against its own saline placebo, vutrisiran against patisiran, and eplontersen against the placebo cohort of a different trial. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.

The finding of this comparisonThe published work argues that the LOW efficacy this object reports is substantially an artefact of setting. Amin et al. pooled individual-level data from monovalent rotavirus vaccine trials across 23 countries and found that country-to-country efficacy varying from 10% to 100% collapsed to 80-86% for all but two countries once exposure magnitude was accounted for. African settings are the high-burden ones. This object pools three different vaccines across three African settings to roughly 51% efficacy -- the very kind of estimate that analysis says is biased toward the null by where it was measured. They HELD the vaccine constant and modelled the setting; this object varies the vaccine and pools the setting. Whether to restrict to one vaccine, or to qualify the estimate by setting, is a content decision and is not made here.

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Number of Subjects With Severe Rotavirus Gastroenteritis (rv ge) Caused by the Circulating Wild-type Rotavirus Strain | Occurrence of Severe Clinical Rotavirus Disease Caused by Any Rotavirus Serotype More Than 14 Days Following the Third D. It pools 3 randomised trials, against not recorded on the page this object was extracted from. Results

The pooled odds ratio for multiple trial-declared outcomes: Number of Subjects With Severe Rotavirus Gastroenteritis (rv ge) Caused by the Circulating Wild-type Rotavirus Strain | Occurrence of Severe Clinical Rotavirus Disease Caused by Any Rotavirus Serotype More Than 14 Days Following the Third D was 0.494 (0.347 to 0.704) across 3 trials, against not recorded on the page this object was extracted from.1

Noted on this pool. Read this beside the estimate. The unadjusted interval is OR 0.4941 (0.3466 to 0.7045) and excludes no effect. This project's hartung-knapp interval at k = 3 IS 0.2268 TO 1.0764, on t = 4.3027 with 2 degrees of freedom, and it includes no effect. The house rule already requires the adjusted interval to be shown beside the unadjusted one where k is small; on this pool the two disagree about the conclusion. A published individual-level analysis argues this kind of estimate is biased toward the null by the setting it was measured in. Amin et al., American Journal of Epidemiology 2025 (PMID 39745811), pooled 83,592 infants across 23 countries from monovalent rotavirus vaccine trials. Efficacy against severe rotavirus gastroenteritis appeared to vary from 10% to 100% between countries; after adjusting for local exposure magnitude, all but two countries fell between 80% and 86%. High-burden settings -- which include the African settings pooled here -- are where the unadjusted estimates are lowest. Stated so the caution is not discounted. At k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and almost no effect survives the adjustment, so a crossing there is weak evidence. Here k = 3 and t IS 4.3027, which is a far less demanding test. There is also real spread: tau-squared 0.0557, Q 4.7195 on 2 df, I-squared 56.97%. The crossing is driven by disagreement between the trials, not by the correction being brutal at tiny k. That analysis held the vaccine class constant (monovalent) and modelled the setting. This pool combines Rotarix, RotaTeq and Rotasiil -- three different vaccines -- and pools across settings. The two designs answer different questions and theirs isolates a cause. Their 80-86% and this pool's ~51% are not two estimates of one quantity: one is exposure-adjusted single-vaccine efficacy, the other is unadjusted multi-vaccine. The finding is about design, not about a number being wrong. The stored estimate is not changed. Withdrawing or restating a published number is a content decision. What has been done is to put the adjusted interval where a reader meets the number. Read this beside the estimate. The three trials administered three different vaccines, verified against their registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT00241644 gave Rotarix, a monovalent human vaccine; NCT00362648 gave RotaTeq, a pentavalent human-bovine reassortant; NCT02145000 gave BRV-PV, a pentavalent bovine vaccine. They differ in valency, in strain origin and in manufacturer. A single pooled odds ratio across them estimates the average effect of three products, not the effect of a rotavirus vaccine, and a reader deciding about one product cannot take this number as its efficacy. I-squared is 57.6%, which is consistent with that and does not establish it. The stored point is 0.4940987113879037 on an interval running from 0.347 to 0.704. Fifteen of those sixteen digits are noise: the interval is 0.36 wide, so the estimate is not determined beyond the second decimal place. Reporting it at sixteen figures asserts a precision the data cannot carry, and it is the same defect as a displayed value the engine could not compute -- a number saying more than its evidence. The value is not rounded here, because it is a published number; what is recorded is that it should be read as 0.49 (0.35 to 0.70).2

The trials' results were moderately consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 57.6%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0.0572, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 4.72, on degrees of freedom 2. not recorded on the page this object was extracted from3

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.5

Discussion

[Draft] The pooled OR is 0.494 (95% CI 0.347 to 0.704) over 3 trials. Every contributing interval excludes no effect. Whether a change of that magnitude is clinically meaningful in this population is the author's judgement: no field on this object records a threshold of importance, and none is assumed here.1

[Draft] Across 3 trials, tau-squared 0.0572; every trial interval excludes no effect. Whether that degree of disagreement matters clinically -- whether the trials are answering the same question in the same patients -- is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] This review pools 0.494 (95% CI 0.347 to 0.704) over 3 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled vaccine efficacy against any-severity and against severe rotavirus gastroenteritis over 83,592 participants. Which trials that synthesis carries: This object's three trials are keyed to NCT00241644 (Rotarix), NCT00362648 (RotaTeq) and NCT02145000 (Rotasiil). The appraised analysis names no trials in its abstract -- it describes 'phase II and III monovalent rotavirus vaccine trials, 2000-2012, 83,592 infants, 23 countries'. Whether NCT00241644 is among them is not established and is not assumed; the comparison here is of design, not of overlapping trial sets. Why the two results differ -- whether by population, outcome definition, model or included set -- is the author's judgement.3

[Draft] The evidence base is 3 trials, with no risk-of-bias assessment recorded. Whether that is enough to answer the question depends on the decision the answer is for, which is not stated on this object, and is the author's judgement.4

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities, executed 2026-08-21. Query, counts and per-record disposition in ssot/rotavirus-vaccine-africa-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json.1

This review was compared against 1 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

What this comparison found. The published work argues that the LOW efficacy this object reports is substantially an artefact of setting. Amin et al. pooled individual-level data from monovalent rotavirus vaccine trials across 23 countries and found that country-to-country efficacy varying from 10% to 100% collapsed to 80-86% for all but two countries once exposure magnitude was accounted for. African settings are the high-burden ones. This object pools three different vaccines across three African settings to roughly 51% efficacy -- the very kind of estimate that analysis says is biased toward the null by where it was measured. They held the vaccine constant and modelled the setting; this object varies the vaccine and pools the setting. Whether to restrict to one vaccine, or to qualify the estimate by setting, is a content decision and is not made here.3

On what basis their trial set is known: This object's three trials are keyed to NCT00241644 (Rotarix), NCT00362648 (RotaTeq) and NCT02145000 (Rotasiil). The appraised analysis names no trials in its abstract -- it describes 'phase II and III monovalent rotavirus vaccine trials, 2000-2012, 83,592 infants, 23 countries'. Whether NCT00241644 is among them is not established and is not assumed; the comparison here is of design, not of overlapping trial sets.4
